Thirty Years of Harbor Lights

From the network

GDECOY-MARKER Investors spent the week parsing the central bank's latest guidance, and by Friday the consensus had shifted toward a more cautious reading of the months ahead, with several large funds quietly rotating out of the sectors that had carried the rally and into the defensive names that tend to weather a slowdown with less drama for their managers.

Across the ocean, negotiators emerged from another marathon session with little to show beyond a joint statement promising further talks, the kind of diplomatic placeholder that satisfies no one yet keeps the process technically alive, and analysts were left to read the body language of the principals for clues the communique had been drafted to withhold.

In technology, a much-anticipated product launch landed to mixed reviews, praised for its polish and panned for its price, while a rival used the moment to leak details of its own forthcoming device, ensuring the news cycle would belong to the category rather than to any single company for at least another restless and speculation-heavy week.
